subject: business-studies
title: Taylor, McGregor and McClelland
welcome_lead: From scientific management to Theory X/Y and McClelland's three needs.
meta_desc: A-Level HR: Taylor's scientific management, McGregor X/Y, McClelland.
final_note: Assumptions about workers shape the systems managers build - choose them carefully.

concepts.def: Scientific management - measure, simplify, pay piece rates.
McGregor's view that workers dislike work and need control.
McGregor's view that workers are creative and self-directed.
McClelland's drive to accomplish challenging goals.
McClelland's drive to influence and lead others.

walkthroughs.body_html: Taylor broke jobs into measured steps and rewarded volume with piece rates. It raised output but treated workers as cogs - high turnover and strikes followed in some factories.
Managers who believe Theory X use close supervision and rewards/punishments. Theory Y managers delegate, empower and trust - and tend to get more creativity in return.
McClelland argues people are driven by varying mixes of achievement, affiliation and power. Sales reps often score high on achievement; managers on power; team players on affiliation.

mcqs.q: What do McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y describe?
options: Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
Two contrasting management assumptions: Theory X assumes workers dislike work and need control; Theory Y assumes workers can be self-motivated and seek responsibility.
Theory X is about working in a factory and Theory Y is about office work.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.

mcqs.q: How does HRM differ from traditional personnel management?
options: HRM treats people as a strategic asset and integrates human resource policies with business strategy; personnel management is more administrative and reactive, handling hiring, pay and disputes.
Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
HRM and personnel are exactly the same thing — just a name change.

mcqs.q: What is Taylor's theory of scientific management?
options: Taylor said workers are motivated by recognition and teamwork.
Theory X and Theory Y are stages of business growth.
Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
Workers are motivated primarily by money; efficiency is maximised by breaking tasks into standardised steps, training workers in 'the one best way', and using piece-rate pay.
